A1_SYNC_ACK.summary: SYNC_ACK / SYNC_FINAL_ACK are plaintext kind-25060 contents signed only with a disposable ephemeral Nostr key. Phone advances durable checkpoints and completes sync without verifying D_sign, session AEAD, or binding beyond t=sos-hist-v1 + role!=phone.

codePaths.detail: finalizeEvent(..., ephSk) — not DeviceAuthorization D_sign. SYNC_ACK content is JSON.stringify plaintext.
After flush+checkpoint on desktop, emits plaintext SYNC_ACK with batchId/batchSeq/cursorCommitted.
Comment: 'plaintext desktop control'. On type==SYNC_ACK: acked[batchId]=true AND SosHistoryCheckpointStore.saveAtomic(...). On SYNC_FINAL_ACK: done.countDown().
Accepts any EVENT kind=25060 with t=sos-hist-v1 and role!=localRole. Does not verify Schnorr against D_sign. Does not require AEAD. Does not bind pubkey to authorized desktop.

properties.replayProtectionBeyondSeenEventId: partial (event id de-dupe only; forged new ids accepted)
properties.duplicateAckDoubleAdvance: mitigated for same batchId map entry; forged new batchId+cursor can still advance seq/cursor

minimalCorrectiveDesign: 1. Seal SYNC_ACK / SYNC_FINAL_ACK with the existing hist session AEAD (sessionKey + transcript bind AAD), same as HIST_BATCH — never plaintext control.
2. Optionally also sign ACK payload with D_sign (Schnorr over SOS|hist|ack|v1 || bind || batchId || batchSeq || cursor || exportSessionId) and verify on phone against authorization.D_sign_pub.

3. Phone: reject ACK unless AEAD opens under current sessionKey; require batchId ∈ outstanding in-flight set; require batchSeq == expected; ignore/reject cursor that moves backward or skips without replay window policy.
4. Bind ACK fields: accountP, deviceId, authorizationId, authEpoch, sessionId, exportSessionId.
5. Idempotent: spentAckIds set; duplicate AEAD ciphertext or batchId ACK must not re-save checkpoint.
6. Missing ACK → timeout INTERRUPTED (already present); never invent COMPLETE from silence.
7. Add negative tests: forged plaintext ACK, wrong-session ACK, replayed ACK, ACK without AEAD, ACK with wrong D_sign.

A2_TOMBSTONE_FALLBACK.summary: Raw NIP-44 fallback only replaces chat-e2ee facade parse; ciphertext still requires conversation key from sealed CKI. However desktop import never calls verifyEvent on outer kind-1050 signatures before applying tombstones.

codePaths.detail: On SosChatE2ee failure, nip44.decrypt(ct, ck) then JSON.parse — accepts atypical inners including tombstone markers.
Tombstone allowed if author∈{self,peer}; markDeleted(targetId). No event.sig verification anywhere in HIST_BATCH loop.

preserved: Batch envelope authenticated by hist session AEAD (phone→desktop).
Conversation key comes from D_enc-opened CKI under DeviceAuthorization.
Participant-only tombstone author check; no resurrection after deletedChatMessageIds.
gaps: Outer Nostr event.sig not verified against event.pubkey before deletion applies.
Any holder of conversation key can produce NIP-44 ciphertext that decrypts to {type:tombstone}; without sig check, pubkey attribution is not cryptographically bound to the inner.
minimalCorrectiveDesign: For tombstones: require event.pubkey === original author or self per existing deletion policy; prefer e-tag targetId matching a previously imported event id.
Do not treat facade-rejected payloads as deletions unless verifyEvent + participant policy pass.

A3_TEST_ONLY_KEYS.notes: SosJsBridge has exportConversationKeyIndexSealed only; copyEncPrivateKeyForTests gated by BuildConfig.DEBUG in SosDeviceIdentityStore.

STOP_REASON: A1: unauthenticated SYNC_ACK advances durable phone checkpoints and can forge session completion. Mission forbids implementing attachment sync behind an untrusted completion mechanism.
